goal: Speed up cryptographic signing by using CPU hardware-accelerated SHA256 in libsecp256k1
Provides 7% to 15% faster ECDSA and Schnorr signing on hardware supporting SHA extensions
reviewability: Ready for review following a rebase that resolved conflicts
agreement: Broad concept approval without detailed rationale (fjahr, hebasto, ismaelsadeeq, sedited, theStack, w0xlt)
Code approval noting MuSig and BIP352 could also benefit in follow-up work (theStack)
Resolved suggestion to use a single context after author noted thread-safety reasons (theStack)

categories.name: utils
why: P3 because ECDSA and Schnorr signing gain a modest 7% to 15% speedup on CPUs with SHA extensions
Signing is rarely a node bottleneck and verification performance is essentially unchanged
Enables future performance improvements in BIP352 and MuSig modules
